question: Among all the extensions the states admit, what do uniform rules that read only the states grow (names erased); does the rule or the start supply the number of orders; do the states decide each step or does a coin; is a second order typical or rare under fewest-states, uniform and softmax weightings (extensions counted one by one or classes once); and does a rule that may read which knots meet (from two starts with the same states and different knots) grow differently?

definitions.extension: the states left by adding distinction n with up to K betweenness knots on triples containing n, every old state kept, n constrained and untied
definitions.orders: k = chromatic number of the split crossing graph; lambda = lattice dimension (least chain cover of nested oriented splits); two orders = k = lambda = 2
definitions.D1: the number of classes (up to renaming) among the top-weight options at a step
definitions.knot-local: each new knot's two old distinctions lie together in one existing knot; strict: the whole move's old distinctions in one existing knot; closure: in some betweenness triple every state satisfies

public_inputs.code: rules.py (sha256 7ea310dca857d82506e29a9819339164858fb74c9426a5dae94a6bd177c5ad6c), run.py (sha256 dd2cc72cc5d7413e41b92a2c0cdfdc37b76896ab46ac902bc17b16cee95ed8c8), checks.py (sha256 41ab6b41be229542a08460fe738d12adcb50f8ea1d955f56e54d55cf3e12f2eb); Python 3 with networkx 3.6.1 (the workspace .venv)
public_inputs.run: .venv/bin/python -B run.py --part NAME for each of E6, E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E3c, E7, E8 (each its own process), then run.py --merge; run.py --stress for the stress test

forbidden_inputs: Changing rules, starts, readings, predictions or decision rules after seeing registered results
cheapest_meaningful_control: F1 from the line (a theorem: an exact line every run); states-only and closure-local rules from the two six-starts (identical by construction).

predictions.R3: C(n,3) zero-cost, all two orders, 10/19/28 classes
predictions.R5: F1 line prob 1, one class at the top
predictions.R6: F2 line at n = 4 strictly between 0 and 1
predictions.R7: F3: 2x2 at 4 (one class), two classes 1/2 at 5, two orders 1/2 at 6 and 0 at 7, Q3 at 8
predictions.R8: F3c: two orders 5/12 at 6, Q3 at 8
predictions.R10: F1 conserves (k, lambda) from three starts; line always one class, 2x2 and star not
predictions.R11: F3, F3c: Q3 at 8 and Q4 at 16 in 40/40; top more than one class at a majority of steps from 5
predictions.R12: U1, U3: two orders < 10% at 10, lambda >= 3 majority; U3 k >= 3 majority at 7
predictions.R13: softmax: two orders < half at 10 for every beta
predictions.R14: signed group: one invariant open continuation at the 3-line (parity), none at the 2x2, no invariant knot extension
predictions.R15: global-swap group: one invariant open knot extension at the 2x2, 10 states
predictions.R16: states-only and closure-local identical from the two six-starts
predictions.R17: KF3 exact: 1/2, 1/2 at 5; two orders 2/3 at 6, 0 at 7
predictions.R18: KF3 from one knot: Q3 at 8 in >= 24/30, two orders in none at 12
predictions.R19: KF3 six-starts: 12 states to 12 in >= 24/30; two orders <= 3 at 12; at 8 >= 1 each, counts differ

decision_rules.each prediction: holds or fails as stated in the pre-registration

stop_rule: One run (plus the non-blocking stress test); A97 status; referee hand-off; report.
runtime: Expected under an hour, one process, run in the background; registered in docs/LONG_RUNNING.md if it passes ten minutes.

amendments.before_any_read_out: of E1 beyond F1 and of E2-E8 (E6 and E1's F1 had printed when the first run was stopped)
amendments.change: The first run (one process, parts in order) spent over an hour in E1's exact F2 run to n = 9: under F2 the classes multiply (650 at n = 7, about 9 s; n = 9 would take hours), the time going to isomorphism checks. The run was stopped. run.py now runs each part as its own process (--part NAME, then --merge) so that no part blocks another, and F2's exact run stops at n = 7. R6 (F2 at n = 4) is unaffected. rules.py, the rules, starts, readings, predictions and decision rules are unchanged.

amendments.before_any_read_out: of E2, E3 and E3c (none had printed; E1, E4-E8 had finished with the frozen class graph and are unaffected)
amendments.change: E2, E3 and E3c, which check at every step whether the top options form one class, printed nothing in 27 minutes: the isomorphism search on the incidence graph of distinctions and split sides blows up exponentially as lines grow (32 s for one step at n = 13). They were stopped. rules.py's Canon now compares the complete graph on the distinctions weighted by the disagreement count (with N in the key, and the knots as before); by DISTANCE-ORDER-20261117-001A statement 3(a) the counts and N determine these bases for n >= 4, so the classes are the same. A new check (13) confirms agreement with the frozen graph on 166 pairs of bases. One F3 run to n = 16 now takes under a second. E2, E3 and E3c are rerun from the start; no rule, start, reading, prediction or decision rule changed.
